data.title: Framycetin sulphate 1% cream
data.summary: II Antibacterials · Aminoglycoside antibiotic (closely related to neomycin; neomycin B)
data.body:
_Topicals · II Antibacterials_

**Class:** Aminoglycoside antibiotic (closely related to neomycin; neomycin B)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds the 30S ribosomal subunit → misreading of mRNA → bactericidal
- Active against staphylococci and many Gram-negative bacilli; weak against streptococci

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Superficial bacterial skin infections, infected wounds, burns, ulcers (also as impregnated gauze — tulle dressings)
- Commonly used in India; limited by sensitisation

## Dose & formulations
- Apply 2–3 times daily for up to 7 days; gauze dressings changed daily

## Adverse effects
- Allergic contact dermatitis (common; cross-reacts with neomycin, gentamicin)
- Ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity if absorbed from large raw areas, especially in renal impairment

## Contraindications
- Large raw areas/burns in renal impairment; perforated ear drum (ototoxic)
- Known aminoglycoside allergy

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid on large areas (fetal ototoxicity in theory).

## Viva points
- Aminoglycoside — contact sensitiser (neomycin group) and ototoxic if absorbed
- Suspect allergy if a wound worsens on framycetin tulle

_Sources: Khopkar ch.18; Wolverton 4e ch.41 (neomycin/aminoglycosides) and ch.56 (Irritants and allergens). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
